why: Values and principles vs purpose/context vs compliance, governance, provenance and scope.

options.name: Institutional values and principles for AI use
options.covers: An institution-level framework or preamble stating the purpose, scope, and principles for AI use.

options.name: Purpose and context of the policy document
options.covers: Why the document exists, what problem it addresses and its context (split from P56, which keeps values and principles).

options.name: Existing law and university policy apply to AI
options.covers: AI use must follow laws (records, privacy, IP) and existing university policies (conduct, acceptable use, branding), and violations fall under those policies. Different from P45, which treats AI like a human collaborator under integrity rules. Evidence: Amherst, Boise State, Kansas State, Arizona State, Cal State, Davidson.

options.name: Governance roles, ownership and exceptions
options.covers: Names the office, officer, council or committee that interprets, implements, monitors or enforces the AI policy, or the process for granting exceptions to it. Evidence: Purdue, Rowan, Oakland, Morehouse, Northeastern, Northwestern, Portland State, Santa Clara.

options.name: How the policy was made (body, process, sources, AI assistance)
options.covers: States the process, body or date by which the AI policy or guidance was drafted, consulted on, adopted or ratified. Evidence: New Mexico State, Rice, Northeastern, Santa Clara.

options.name: Definitions and scope of the policy
options.covers: Definitions of AI, generative AI, AI tools or agentic systems that set what a policy covers (sources: Oregon State, Howard).

units.passage: They aim to provide clear and practical guidance for faculty, students, and staff on integrating and using AI technologies in teaching and learning at Old Dominion University (ODU). units.why: The guidelines open by stating purpose and scope for faculty, students and staff, setting an institution-level framework: 'clear and practical guidance for faculty, students, and staff'.

units.passage: Transparency in AI applications is essential.
units.why: "Transparency in AI applications is essential" states a general principle of the framework, so P56 (institution-wide principles) is the fit.

units.passage: The purpose of this policy is to establish a culture of integrity that ensures the responsible, ethical, and transparent use of artificial intelligence (AI) technology in public higher education
units.why: The Purpose section says the policy aims to 'establish a culture of integrity that ensures the responsible, ethical, and transparent use of artificial intelligence', an institution-wide statement of purpose (P56) that applies to everyone in scope.

units.passage: Ensure Ethical Use: Prioritize ethical considerations and ethical use in AI deployment, in teaching, learning, research, and administration, promoting fairness, accountability, transparency and respect for human rights in all AI applications and AI related activities conducted within the University.
units.why: The policy statement commits to 'Ensure Ethical Use' with 'fairness, accountability, transparency and respect for human rights', an ethics principle (P56 framework).

units.passage: True to our liberal arts core , the University of Oregon strives to explore and expand human potential as we integrate AI into our evolving educational mission. In our teaching and learning, we seek to combine the deepest understanding of the human condition with the most sophisticated engagement with technology. Recognizing that all technologies have affordances and limitations, we aim to bring forward critical and holistic perspectives on AI systems and, when appropriate, adopt AI purposefully to enhance the human capacity for ethical, critical, and creative thinking in our students and ourselves.
units.why: The statement of purpose is the Provost-approved "north star" for AI in teaching; it sets purpose and principles ("adopt AI purposefully to enhance the human capacity for ethical, critical, and creative thinking"), so it is an institution-wide framework (P56), informs only.

units.passage: The prevalence of generative AI requires a both/and approach at the University of Oregon: both embracing AI tools to prepare students for their careers and futures and deepening the human skills and relationships that give a liberal arts education its enduring value.
units.why: The same sentence adds "deepening the human skills and relationships that give a liberal arts education its enduring value", a stated priority to protect human skills. No type captures it exactly: not P41 (practice builds skill) or P121 (displacement), so UNCOVERED.

units.passage: The guidance developed by the workgroup, with feedback from key OSU stakeholders, is designed to reflect OSU's shared commitments to human cognition and creativity, academic integrity, and inclusive excellence; support faculty autonomy and intellectual freedom; and maintain transparency, uphold our ethical responsibilities as educators, and protect the privacy and security of individual and institutional data.
units.why: The memo says the guidance aims to 'protect the privacy and security of individual and institutional data', a privacy principle for AI use. P50 fits since it concerns data protection; it informs.

units.passage: This statement establishes shared expectations for AI use across EECS courses so as to set clear expectations. While individual faculty will set course-specific rules, this document provides the common floor and vocabulary.
units.why: The introduction says the statement 'establishes shared expectations for AI use across EECS courses' and 'provides the common floor and vocabulary' while faculty set course rules. A unit-level framework: P56.

units.passage: The guidance developed by the workgroup, with feedback from key OSU stakeholders, is designed to reflect OSU's shared commitments to human cognition and creativity, academic integrity, and inclusive excellence; support faculty autonomy and intellectual freedom; and maintain transparency, uphold our ethical responsibilities as educators, and protect the privacy and security of individual and institutional data.
units.why: The memo says the guidance reflects 'shared commitments to human cognition and creativity, academic integrity, and inclusive excellence', which states the principles behind the university framework. It is P56 because it is an institution-level preamble, and it informs rather than directs.

units.passage: that integration must reflect our shared commitments to human cognition and creativity, academic integrity, and inclusive excellence
units.why: The guidance says AI integration 'must reflect our shared commitments to human cognition and creativity, academic integrity, and inclusive excellence', an institution-level principle statement, so P56.

units.passage: The Center for Teaching and Learning (CTL) supports an ethic of transparency around the use of generative AI in teaching and learning,
units.why: CTL 'supports an ethic of transparency around the use of generative AI in teaching and learning', a principle statement that sets the purpose of the guidance (P56).

units.passage: Penn State supports the responsible exploration and use of AI.
units.why: The opening line sets the university's stance: 'supports the responsible exploration and use of AI', a framework-level principle rather than a rule, so P56 with informs.

units.passage: These general guidelines provide a shared foundation to help the Penn State community make informed decisions when using AI tools.
units.why: States the scope and purpose of the guidelines ('a shared foundation... informed decisions'), which is a framework preamble (P56); it leaves decisions to individuals.

units.passage: Pepperdine University recognizes the prevalence of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and services and their potential impact — positive, negative, and neutral — on the academic community.
units.why: The overview frames AI as having "positive, negative, and neutral" impact and sets the purpose of the guidance; this is a preamble of principle, so P56 and modality informs.

units.passage: The Committee urges that these Points to Consider be employed when implementing its Recommendations.
units.why: "The Committee urges that these Points to Consider be employed when implementing its Recommendations." It recommends a framework for implementing the institution's recommendations, so P56, should.

units.passage: Points to Consider in addressing concerns or developing policy regarding GenAI ( §5 ).
units.why: The report offers "Points to Consider in addressing concerns or developing policy regarding GenAI". It describes the institution-wide framework the report contains, so P56, informs.

units.passage: To provide a unified system and increase clarity about what AI usages are allowed or disallowed across all Pomona Computer Science classes.
units.why: States the purpose is 'a unified system' to clarify allowed and disallowed AI uses 'across all Pomona Computer Science classes'. It is a department-level preamble giving purpose and scope, so P56 and informs; the tier structure itself is coded in a later unit as P05.

units.passage: PCC embraces emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), to the extent that they advance this mission and our shared values
units.why: The opening sentence sets the college's institutional stance: PCC 'embraces emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI)', but only 'to the extent that they advance this mission'. That is a framework statement for all of PCC (all, general, informs), so P56; it welcomes AI conditionally, hence permit.

units.passage: AI may enhance teaching and learning, but it must do so in ways that center students, uphold equity, and respect the professional judgment of faculty
units.why: The sentence sets conditions on AI: it "must do so in ways that center students, uphold equity, and respect the professional judgment of faculty". It is a principle in the institutional framework (P56); equity (P51) is only one of three principles so P56 fits best.

units.passage: Portland State University’s AI Working Group embraces responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) as a transformative tool to enhance teaching, learning, and research. We view AI not as a replacement for human intellect, but as a catalyst for innovation that requires thoughtful, human-centered oversight.
units.why: The opening sentence states the institution's position that it "embraces responsible use" of AI as a tool for teaching, learning and research; this is a framework preamble (P56), and the welcome gives it an encouraging stance.

units.passage: Portland State University understands that artificial intelligence (AI) brings both opportunities and risks to student learning.
units.why: The page says the university "understands that artificial intelligence (AI) brings both opportunities and risks to student learning," a framing statement that gives no rule.

units.passage: Propósito Esta Política tiene el propósito de establecer los principios para el uso responsable y ético de la tecnología de la IA, en las áreas administrativas, académicas y de investigación. B.
units.policy: The Policy's purpose is to establish the principles for responsible and ethical use of AI technology in administrative, academic and research areas.
units.why: The purpose clause says the policy exists "para establecer los principios para el uso responsable y ético" of AI in administrative, academic and research areas, which is an institution-wide framework statement (P56).

units.passage: ARTÍCULO II – RESUMEN EJECUTIVO La Universidad de Puerto Rico (en adelante, la Universidad), en su misión de educar y forjar profesionales que aportan a la sociedad de forma técnica, científica y cultural, se preocupa por el uso ético y responsable de la inteligencia artificial (en adelante, la IA) en todas sus modalidades.
units.policy: The University is concerned with the ethical and responsible use of AI in all its modalities.
units.why: The executive summary frames the University's concern for "el uso ético y responsable de la inteligencia artificial" in all modalities; it is a preamble of principle, so P56.

units.why: Principle 2 says the University "se compromete a asumir la responsabilidad" for developing and using AI under ethical and legal standards; a principle, so P56.

units.why: Principle 5 commits to respect for "derechos fundamentales, así como los derechos humanos" and encourages AI use consistent with them; a framework principle, P56.
